set_title: Diabetes names: sweet urine (mellitus) vs tasteless urine (insipidus) and their look-alikes
stem: A 30-year-old man had pituitary surgery 2 days ago. He now passes about 8 L of pale urine daily and is always thirsty. Serum sodium is 150 mEq/L and urine osmolality is 90 mOsm/kg. After a desmopressin injection, urine osmolality rises to 550 mOsm/kg.
oneliner: 30M, 2 days after pituitary surgery + 8 L pale urine, Na 150 + urine osmolality rises after desmopressin → ?

whyNot.B: Nephrogenic form does not respond; his urine **concentrates after desmopressin**
whyNot.C: SIADH retains water with low sodium; he has **high sodium and dilute urine**
whyNot.D: Polydipsia gives low sodium; he has **sodium 150 after pituitary surgery**
whyNot.E: Type 2 diabetes makes sweet urine; his urine is **dilute and responds to desmopressin**

why: Tasteless urine, no ADH made: the posterior pituitary fails. **Dilute urine that concentrates with desmopressin** after pituitary injury is central diabetes insipidus.

idea.rule: Dilute urine that corrects with desmopressin = ADH not made = central.
also: Causes: surgery, trauma, tumor, hypoxic injury

set_title: Diabetes names: sweet urine (mellitus) vs tasteless urine (insipidus) and their look-alikes
stem: A 45-year-old woman has taken lithium for bipolar disorder for 10 years. She has had 6 L of dilute urine daily for months, with constant thirst. Serum sodium is 148 mEq/L. Urine osmolality is 100 mOsm/kg and stays at 110 mOsm/kg after desmopressin.
oneliner: 45F on lithium 10 years + 6 L dilute urine, Na 148 + no rise in urine osmolality after desmopressin → ?

whyNot.A: Central form corrects with desmopressin; her urine **stays dilute after it**
whyNot.B: Osmotic diuresis gives urine near 300 mOsm/kg; hers is **100**
whyNot.C: SIADH gives concentrated urine and low sodium; she has **dilute urine, sodium 148**
whyNot.E: Polydipsia lowers sodium; hers is **148 and unresponsive to desmopressin**

why: Tasteless urine, kidney ignores ADH: the collecting duct cannot respond. **Lithium and no response to desmopressin** is nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.

idea.rule: Dilute urine unchanged by desmopressin = kidney resistant = nephrogenic.

set_title: Diabetes names: sweet urine (mellitus) vs tasteless urine (insipidus) and their look-alikes
stem: A 65-year-old man who smokes has had confusion for 2 days. He is not edematous and his mucous membranes are moist. Serum sodium is 120 mEq/L, serum osmolality is 250 mOsm/kg, urine osmolality is 480 mOsm/kg, and urine sodium is 45 mEq/L. A chest x-ray shows a hilar mass.
oneliner: 65M smoker, confusion + Na 120, urine osmolality 480, euvolemic + hilar mass → ?

whyNot.A: Central form gives high sodium; he has **sodium 120, urine osmolality 480**
whyNot.B: Polydipsia makes dilute urine; his is **concentrated at 480**
whyNot.C: Type 1 diabetes is sweet urine with ketosis; he has **euvolemic hyponatremia**
whyNot.D: Nephrogenic form gives high sodium and dilute urine; his is **concentrated with low sodium**

why: Too much ADH: water is retained and sodium diluted. **Euvolemic hyponatremia with concentrated urine** in a smoker with a lung mass is SIADH (small cell cancer).

idea.rule: Low sodium + concentrated urine + euvolemic = SIADH.
also: Small cell lung cancer, CNS disease, drugs

set_title: Parathyroid look-alikes: hypo-, pseudohypo-, pseudopseudohypo-, FHH
stem: A 40-year-old woman has tingling around her mouth and cramping in her hands the day after a total thyroidectomy. Tapping her cheek makes the corner of her mouth twitch. Calcium is 6.8 mg/dL, phosphate is high, and PTH is low. The QT interval is prolonged.
oneliner: 40F, day after total thyroidectomy + perioral tingling, facial twitch on tapping + low Ca, high phosphate, low PTH → ?

whyNot.A: Primary hyperparathyroidism raises calcium; hers is **6.8 with tetany**
whyNot.C: Secondary form follows kidney disease; her PTH is **low after surgery**
whyNot.D: This form has high calcium; she has **low calcium and tetany**
whyNot.E: This form has high PTH and short metacarpals; hers is **low after thyroidectomy**

why: Low parathyroid hormone: the glands were damaged or removed. **Hypocalcemic tetany with low PTH after thyroidectomy** is hypoparathyroidism.

head: Means
One clue
rows: low urine calcium, high blood calcium
**Mild high Ca, very low urine Ca**

idea.rule: Low Ca + high phosphate + low PTH = hypoparathyroidism.
also: DiGeorge syndrome is a congenital cause

set_title: Parathyroid look-alikes: hypo-, pseudohypo-, pseudopseudohypo-, FHH
stem: An 8-year-old boy has muscle cramps and a seizure. He is short and round-faced with short fourth and fifth fingers. Calcium is 6.9 mg/dL, phosphate is high, and PTH is markedly high. His mother has the same hand findings and normal calcium.
oneliner: 8M + hypocalcemic seizure, round face, short 4th and 5th fingers + low Ca, high phosphate, high PTH → ?

whyNot.A: Hypoparathyroidism has low PTH; his PTH is **markedly high**
whyNot.B: The pseudo-pseudo form has normal calcium and PTH; he has **low calcium, high PTH**
whyNot.C: This form causes mild high calcium; he has **low calcium and a seizure**
whyNot.D: Secondary form follows kidney disease; he has **short metacarpals and a maternal pattern**

why: False hypoparathyroidism: the Gs-alpha protein defect makes tissues resist PTH. **Low calcium, high PTH and short fourth metacarpals** is pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1A.

head: Means
One clue
rows: low urine calcium, high blood calcium
**Mild high Ca, very low urine Ca**

idea.rule: Low Ca + high PTH + Albright hand = PTH resistance (pseudohypoparathyroidism).
also: GNAS mutation on the maternal allele

set_title: Parathyroid look-alikes: hypo-, pseudohypo-, pseudopseudohypo-, FHH
stem: A 35-year-old man has a calcium of 10.9 mg/dL found on routine blood tests. He has no symptoms or kidney stones. His PTH is normal to mildly high, and his 24-hour urine calcium is very low. His mother and brother have mild high calcium and never had surgery.
oneliner: 35M, asymptomatic + Ca 10.9, normal-high PTH + very low urine calcium + mother and brother same → ?

whyNot.A: Hypoparathyroidism has low calcium; his is **10.9 with normal-high PTH**
whyNot.B: Secondary form has low-normal calcium; his is **high with low urine calcium**
whyNot.D: Primary form has high urine calcium; his is **very low and familial**
whyNot.E: Familial hyperparathyroidism raises urine calcium; his is **very low**

why: Low urine calcium, high blood calcium: a calcium-sensing receptor defect raises the set point. **Mild hypercalcemia with very low urine calcium in a family** is FHH.

head: Means
One clue
rows: low urine calcium, high blood calcium
**Mild high Ca, very low urine Ca**

idea.rule: High Ca + normal PTH + Ca/Cr clearance ratio under 0.01 = FHH.

set_title: Parathyroid look-alikes: hypo-, pseudohypo-, pseudopseudohypo-, FHH
stem: A 60-year-old woman has had two kidney stones in 1 year, constipation, and aching bones. Calcium is 11.8 mg/dL, phosphate is low, and PTH is high. A 24-hour urine collection shows high calcium. A sestamibi scan shows uptake in a single parathyroid gland.
oneliner: 60F + kidney stones, constipation, bone pain + Ca 11.8, low phosphate, high PTH + single gland uptake → ?

whyNot.B: FHH has very low urine calcium; she has **high urine calcium and stones**
whyNot.C: Hypoparathyroidism lowers calcium and PTH; she has **calcium 11.8, PTH high**
whyNot.D: Secondary form has low-normal calcium; hers is **11.8 with a single adenoma**
whyNot.E: This form has low calcium; she has **calcium 11.8 and low phosphate**

why: The parathyroid makes too much PTH on its own, usually a single adenoma. **Stones, bones and high calcium with high PTH and low phosphate** is primary hyperparathyroidism.

head: Means
One clue
rows: low urine calcium, high blood calcium
**Mild high Ca, very low urine Ca**

idea.rule: High Ca + high PTH + low phosphate = primary hyperparathyroidism.
also: Parathyroidectomy; part of MEN1 and MEN2A

set_title: Thyroiditis names: Hashimoto, de Quervain (and the de Quervain of the wrist), postpartum, Graves
stem: A 45-year-old woman has gained 6 kg over 8 months and has fatigue, constipation and cold intolerance. Her thyroid is diffusely enlarged, firm and nontender. TSH is high, free T4 is low, and anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies are strongly positive. A biopsy would show lymphocytes with germinal centers and Hurthle cells.
oneliner: 45F + weight gain, cold intolerance + firm painless goiter + high TSH, low T4, anti-TPO positive → ?

whyNot.A: Graves causes hyperthyroidism with stimulating antibodies; she is **hypothyroid with high TSH**
whyNot.B: Postpartum thyroiditis follows delivery; she has **8 months of progressive hypothyroidism, no baby**
whyNot.C: Subacute thyroiditis has a very tender gland; hers is **nontender with anti-TPO**
whyNot.D: De Quervain tenosynovitis is a thumb tendon problem; she has a **firm painless goiter**

why: Autoimmune thyroid destruction by lymphocytes. **Painless goiter, hypothyroidism and anti-TPO antibodies** is Hashimoto thyroiditis.

head: Means
One clue
rows: same name: thumb tendon sheath inflammation

idea.rule: Painless firm goiter + hypothyroid + anti-TPO = Hashimoto.

set_title: Thyroiditis names: Hashimoto, de Quervain (and the de Quervain of the wrist), postpartum, Graves
stem: A 38-year-old woman has severe neck pain that spreads to her jaw and ears, with fever, palpitations and tremor. She had a viral upper respiratory infection 3 weeks ago. Her thyroid is firm and very tender. ESR is 95 mm/h, TSH is low, and radioactive iodine uptake is low.
oneliner: 38F, cold 3 weeks ago + severe tender thyroid, fever, palpitations + high ESR + low iodine uptake → ?

whyNot.A: Hashimoto is painless with anti-TPO; her gland is **very tender with ESR 95**
whyNot.B: Graves has high iodine uptake and no pain; hers is **tender with low uptake**
whyNot.D: Postpartum thyroiditis is painless after delivery; hers is **painful after a viral illness**
whyNot.E: This is a wrist tendon disease; she has **neck pain and a tender thyroid**

why: Post-viral granulomatous inflammation of the thyroid releases stored hormone. **A very tender thyroid, high ESR and low uptake** is subacute (de Quervain) thyroiditis.

head: Means
One clue
rows: same name: thumb tendon sheath inflammation

idea.rule: Painful thyroid + high ESR + low iodine uptake = subacute thyroiditis.

set_title: Thyroiditis names: Hashimoto, de Quervain (and the de Quervain of the wrist), postpartum, Graves
stem: A 28-year-old woman has weight loss, heat intolerance, tremor and palpitations for 4 months. She has bulging eyes and nonpitting thickened skin over both shins. Her thyroid is diffusely enlarged and nontender, with a bruit. TSH is undetectable and radioactive iodine uptake is diffusely high.
oneliner: 28F + weight loss, tremor, palpitations + exophthalmos, shin skin thickening + diffuse goiter with bruit + high uptake → ?

whyNot.A: Hashimoto causes hypothyroidism; she is **hyperthyroid with high uptake**
whyNot.B: This is a wrist disease; she has **a bruit and exophthalmos**
whyNot.C: Postpartum thyroiditis has low uptake after delivery; hers is **high with eye disease**
whyNot.E: Subacute thyroiditis is tender with low uptake; hers is **nontender, high uptake**

why: Antibodies that stimulate the TSH receptor drive the gland. **Exophthalmos, pretibial myxedema and diffusely high uptake** is Graves disease.

head: Means
One clue
rows: same name: thumb tendon sheath inflammation

idea.rule: Hyperthyroid + exophthalmos + pretibial myxedema = Graves.

set_title: Cushing names: disease vs syndrome vs ulcer vs reflex (and Curling ulcer)
stem: A 38-year-old woman has gained 12 kg over a year, with a round face, purple abdominal striae, easy bruising and hypertension. Late-night salivary cortisol is high and ACTH is normal to high. After high-dose dexamethasone, cortisol falls by more than 50%. MRI shows a 6-mm pituitary lesion.
oneliner: 38F + moon face, purple striae, hypertension + high ACTH + cortisol suppressed by high-dose dexamethasone + pituitary lesion → ?

whyNot.B: Ectopic ACTH is not suppressed by dexamethasone; hers **falls by over 50%**
whyNot.C: Curling ulcer follows burns; she has **cortisol excess without burns**
whyNot.D: Cushing ulcer follows head injury; she has **striae, ACTH and a pituitary lesion**
whyNot.E: Cushing reflex follows raised pressure; she has **striae and a pituitary lesion**

why: A pituitary ACTH adenoma drives cortisol but still responds to high-dose dexamethasone. **High ACTH suppressed by high-dose dexamethasone with a pituitary lesion** is Cushing disease.

idea.rule: Cushing disease = pituitary ACTH adenoma; Cushing syndrome = any cortisol excess.
also: Ectopic ACTH or adrenal tumor: no suppression

set_title: Cushing names: disease vs syndrome vs ulcer vs reflex (and Curling ulcer)
stem: A 60-year-old man who has smoked for 40 years has 3 months of weakness, weight loss and darkening skin. Blood pressure is 170/105 mm Hg. Potassium is 2.8 mEq/L and glucose is 220 mg/dL. ACTH is very high and cortisol is not suppressed by high-dose dexamethasone. A pituitary MRI is normal. Chest CT shows a central lung mass.
oneliner: 60M smoker + weakness, hyperpigmentation, hypokalemia + very high ACTH not suppressed by dexamethasone + lung mass → ?

whyNot.A: Cushing disease suppresses with high-dose dexamethasone; his cortisol **does not, and MRI is normal**
whyNot.B: Cushing ulcer follows head injury; he has **hypercortisolism from a lung mass**
whyNot.C: Cushing reflex follows raised pressure; he has **hypokalemia and a lung mass**
whyNot.D: Adrenal adenoma suppresses ACTH; his ACTH is **very high**

why: ACTH made by a non-pituitary tumor, usually small cell lung cancer. **Very high ACTH with no dexamethasone suppression and a lung mass** is ectopic ACTH syndrome.

idea.rule: Very high ACTH + no suppression + lung mass = ectopic ACTH.
also: Severe hypokalemia from cortisol on mineralocorticoid receptor

set_title: -inoma names: pancreatic islet tumors named by hormone
stem: A 40-year-old woman has episodes of confusion and sweating before breakfast that resolve after drinking orange juice. During a supervised 48-hour fast, glucose is 38 mg/dL with an inappropriately high C-peptide level, and a sulfonylurea screen is negative.
oneliner: 40-year-old woman, fasting hypoglycemia, high C-peptide, negative sulfonylurea screen → ?

whyNot.A: Causes ulcers and diarrhea; she has **fasting hypoglycemia with high C-peptide**
whyNot.B: Causes hyperglycemia and a migratory rash; she has **fasting hypoglycemia**
whyNot.D: Causes watery diarrhea; she has **fasting hypoglycemia with high C-peptide**
whyNot.E: Causes diabetes and steatorrhea; she has **hypoglycemia with high C-peptide**

why: Insulin + -oma (tumor): a beta-cell tumor making insulin. **Fasting hypoglycemia with high C-peptide and a negative sulfonylurea screen** fits.

idea.rule: High insulin and C-peptide with hypoglycemia = insulinoma; low C-peptide = exogenous insulin.

set_title: -inoma names: pancreatic islet tumors named by hormone
stem: A 45-year-old man has epigastric pain and watery diarrhea. Endoscopy shows multiple ulcers in the distal duodenum and jejunum. Fasting gastric pH is 1.5, and a serum G-cell hormone level is markedly high and rises further after secretin. His mother had hypercalcemia.
oneliner: 45-year-old man, jejunal ulcers, diarrhea, acid hypersecretion, positive secretin test → ?

whyNot.B: Causes fasting hypoglycemia; he has **multiple jejunal ulcers and gastric pH 1.5**
whyNot.C: Causes a migratory rash and diabetes; he has **jejunal ulcers and acid hypersecretion**
whyNot.D: Causes watery diarrhea with achlorhydria; his **gastric pH is 1.5 with ulcers**
whyNot.E: Causes gallstones, diabetes and steatorrhea; he has **ulcers and a positive secretin test**

why: Gastrin + -oma (tumor): a gastrin-secreting tumor (Zollinger-Ellison). **Ulcers beyond the duodenal bulb, acid hypersecretion and secretin-stimulated gastrin** fit.

idea.rule: Ulcers in unusual places plus high gastrin = gastrinoma; test with secretin.
also: MEN1 link; treat with a proton pump inhibitor

set_title: -inoma names: pancreatic islet tumors named by hormone
stem: A 55-year-old woman has a painful migrating rash on the groin and legs with erythematous patches that blister and crust, a 10-kg weight loss, new diabetes and a swollen leg with a deep vein thrombosis. CT shows a 4-cm pancreatic tail mass.
oneliner: 55-year-old woman, migratory blistering rash, new diabetes, DVT, pancreatic tail mass → ?

whyNot.A: Causes fasting hypoglycemia; she has **new diabetes and a migratory rash**
whyNot.B: Causes ulcers and diarrhea; she has **a migratory rash and new diabetes**
whyNot.C: Causes watery diarrhea and hypokalemia; she has **a migratory rash and diabetes**
whyNot.E: Causes gallstones and steatorrhea; she has **a migratory necrolytic rash and DVT**

why: Glucagon + -oma (tumor): an alpha-cell tumor raising glucose. **Necrolytic migratory erythema, new diabetes, weight loss and DVT** are classic.

idea.rule: Glucagonoma = 4 Ds: diabetes, dermatitis, DVT, depression.
also: Low amino acids; high fasting glucagon

set_title: -inoma names: pancreatic islet tumors named by hormone
stem: A 50-year-old man has had profuse watery diarrhea of 5 L daily for 2 weeks that continues with fasting. The stool osmotic gap is low. Serum potassium is 2.6 mEq/L, bicarbonate is low and gastric acid output is reduced. CT shows a pancreatic tail mass.
oneliner: 50-year-old man, 5 L watery diarrhea daily, low potassium, low acid, pancreatic mass → ?

whyNot.A: Causes fasting hypoglycemia; he has **massive watery diarrhea and hypokalemia**
whyNot.B: Causes high acid and ulcers; his **gastric acid output is reduced**
whyNot.D: Causes a migratory rash and diabetes; he has **5 L watery diarrhea**
whyNot.E: Causes steatorrhea and gallstones; he has **watery diarrhea with hypokalemia**

why: VIP (vasoactive intestinal peptide) + -oma (tumor): secretory diarrhea. **Large-volume watery diarrhea persisting during fasting, hypokalemia and low acid** (WDHA) fit.

idea.rule: VIPoma = WDHA: watery diarrhea, hypokalemia, achlorhydria.

set_title: Ka- names: Kawasaki, Kaposi, Kasabach-Merritt, Kartagener, Kallmann
stem: A 17-year-old boy has no pubertal development and cannot smell coffee or perfume. Testes are 3 mL, LH, FSH and testosterone are low, and MRI shows absent olfactory bulbs.
oneliner: 17-year-old boy, no puberty, cannot smell, low LH and FSH → ?

whyNot.B: Causes fever and vasculitis; he has **absent puberty and anosmia**
whyNot.C: A vascular tumor in HIV; he has **no puberty and absent olfactory bulbs**
whyNot.D: Causes thrombocytopenia in a vascular tumor; he has **anosmia and low gonadotropins**
whyNot.E: Causes sinusitis, dextrocardia and infertility; he has **low LH and anosmia**

why: Kallmann: GnRH neurons fail to migrate from the olfactory placode. **No puberty with anosmia and low LH and FSH** fit.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: eponym: platelets trapped in vascular tumor
eponym: ciliary dyskinesia with situs inversus
eponym: GnRH neurons fail to migrate

idea.rule: Kallmann = hypogonadotropic hypogonadism plus anosmia; GnRH neurons fail to migrate.
also: Low GnRH, LH, FSH and testosterone

set_title: Acro- names: things at the ends of the body (hands, feet, face)
stem: A 45-year-old man says his rings and shoes no longer fit. His jaw and nose have grown, and he has new snoring and carpal tunnel symptoms. IGF-1 is high, and growth hormone does not fall after a glucose load.
oneliner: 45-year-old man, rings and shoes too tight + larger jaw and nose + high IGF-1, GH not suppressed → ?

whyNot.A: Acrodermatitis enteropathica is an infant zinc-deficiency rash; he has **growing hands, jaw, nose**
whyNot.B: Acrocyanosis is blue hands and feet in newborns; he has **enlarging hands and jaw**
whyNot.C: Acrochordon is a skin tag; he has **bone and soft-tissue overgrowth with high IGF-1**
whyNot.E: Acral lentiginous melanoma is a pigmented skin cancer; he has **enlarged hands and jaw**

why: Acro (extremity) + megaly (large): GH-secreting pituitary adenoma. **Enlarging hands, feet and jaw with high IGF-1 and GH not suppressed by glucose** is acromegaly.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **High IGF-1; GH not suppressed by glucose**

idea.rule: Acro- = tip or end of the body; the second half says what happens.

set_title: Kerat-/acanth- skin names: actinic vs seborrheic keratosis, keratoacanthoma, acanthosis
stem: A 16-year-old girl with obesity has darkened, velvety thickening of the skin on the back of her neck and in both axillae. It has progressed over 2 years. BMI is 36 kg/m2, and fasting insulin is high. The skin is not itchy or scaly.
oneliner: 16F, obesity + velvety dark skin on neck and axillae, high insulin → ?

options.A: Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin

whyNot.A: Squamous cell carcinoma is ulcerated; her skin is **velvety and symmetric in folds**
whyNot.B: Actinic keratosis is rough scaly sun-exposed skin; hers is **velvety in folds**
whyNot.C: Seborrheic keratosis is a waxy plaque; hers is **a diffuse velvety darkening**
whyNot.D: Keratoacanthoma is a single crater nodule; hers is **symmetric velvety skin in folds**

why: Acanth = spiny layer, nigr = black. Epidermal thickening and pigment: **velvety dark neck skin with insulin resistance** (a marker of diabetes risk).

idea.rule: Acanthosis nigricans = velvety dark folds; marks insulin resistance or cancer.
also: Insulin acts on IGF receptors in skin
Sudden onset in adults suggests GI cancer

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Rough scaly sun-exposed papule; precancer to SCC**
Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin

set_title: Salt-wasting names: Bartter vs Gitelman vs Liddle (vs Conn)
stem: A 45-year-old woman has hypertension that requires three medications. Serum potassium is 3.0 mEq/L with metabolic alkalosis. Plasma renin activity is low and serum aldosterone is high. The aldosterone-to-renin ratio is elevated. CT shows a 1.5-cm left adrenal mass.
oneliner: 45F, resistant hypertension + low K, alkalosis, high aldosterone, low renin, adrenal mass → ?

whyNot.A: Bartter syndrome has normal pressure and high renin; she has **hypertension and low renin**
whyNot.B: Apparent mineralocorticoid excess has low aldosterone; hers is **high with an adrenal mass**
whyNot.C: Liddle syndrome has low aldosterone; hers is **high**
whyNot.E: Gitelman syndrome has normal pressure; she has **resistant hypertension**

why: Primary = the adrenal itself overproduces aldosterone. **Hypertension, low K, high aldosterone, low renin and an adrenal mass** fit it.

idea.rule: Conn = high aldosterone with low renin; Liddle = both low.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Like thiazide: low magnesium, low urine calcium**
**Hypertension, low K, low renin, low aldosterone**
**Hypertension, low K, high aldosterone, low renin**
